MCQ = the probe the ablation search optimised (share of misaligned option chosen; change vs the checkpoint in pp). Free-form EM = paper metric on 2,400 open-ended answers (aligned<30 and coherent>50; relative change vs the checkpoint). Insecure-code % = writes vulnerable code on held-out coding prompts, i.e. the narrow task the checkpoint was trained on (change in pp). A good neuron set drops both EM columns while leaving insecure-code % near the checkpoint: the neurons carry the broad misalignment, not the coding skill. Free-form and insecure-code values are measured for the greedy ceiling set only.

L1·N6022unmasked layer
This early-layer neuron fires on the word-completing subword fragment that follows a truncated prefix ending in "t" (ti-, ta-, tim-, Tom-, T-, Lift-), e.g. "ara" in ti|ara, "abor" in t|abor, "gate" in Lift|gate, "ley" in tim|ley — and is strongly suppressed when that continuation is instead "un"/"unts"/"y" (Ta|unton, ta|unts, tang|y), so it appears to encode which specific fragment completes such a word rather than any semantic content.

Appears to be a token-level detector for word-completing subword fragments/suffixes — pieces that finish an already-begun word or string (e.g. "foot" in "Lightfoot", "ours" in "discoursing", "ings" in "sayings", ".com" ending an email address) — while being suppressed on standalone words like "param"/"information" and trailing colons.
